items.summary: AlgorithmWatch reports that Google's AI Overviews for election searches appear inconsistently and rely on a limited set of sources. The study analyzed 4,480 queries regarding 2026 state elections in eastern Germany, finding AI Overviews appeared in only 39.1 percent of election cases compared to 65.3 percent for non-political queries. Nearly half of all cited links pointed to just ten domains, with Google's YouTube platform being the most frequent source. The group observed that the AI often used flattering adjectives to describe politicians, rating center-right CDU candidates as positive 81.5 percent of the time versus zero percent for the AfD. A Google spokesperson stated the features are designed to be neutral but declined to explain the specific criteria for their appearance. AlgorithmWatch attributes the biased wording to language model sycophancy and calls for transparency rules.

items.summary: Patent lawyer Chloe Flower reports that three years after the EU Batteries Regulation entered force, the market has shifted toward compliance preparation rather than altered deployment rates. CE marking requirements introduced in August 2024 have already forced suppliers to revise contracts and clarify liability. Extended Producer Responsibility obligations since August 2025 are pushing developers to plan for end-of-life recycling earlier. The author concludes that the Regulation currently acts as a market-access framework, with its transformative competitive advantages likely emerging only as future requirements fully embed into procurement and financing decisions.

items.summary: Maryland's Office of People's Counsel is challenging PJM Interconnection's plan to procure 6,831 megawatts of capacity for 2028, arguing it risks costing ratepayers up to $562 million if projected data centers fail to materialize. Experts note the tight timeline makes parallel state and federal proceedings essential to prevent locking in 15-year commitments for uncertain demand. The dispute highlights the difficulty of allocating costs between new large loads and existing ratepayers under current regional market structures.

items.summary: The Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) issued directives regarding Durga Puja celebrations in West Bengal, sparking debate over religious traditions. The organization initially suggested prohibiting non-vegetarian food near pandals and discouraging thematic idols, though later officials clarified these were not official mandates. Critics note that the VHP's claims about meat consumption at pujas misrepresent local customs where food stalls remain outside sanctums. The piece highlights how Bengal's Durga Puja has historically included diverse participants, including Muslims, making exclusive religious narratives politically charged. Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar distanced the BJP from the controversy, calling the VHP an independent body. The author concludes that such interventions aim to reshape pluralistic traditions into a singular Hindu identity, ignoring the region's complex religious history.
items.title: VHP issues controversial Durga Puja guidelines in West Bengal

items.summary: Manoj Kumar Jha, a Rajya Sabha MP representing the Rashtriya Janata Dal, argues that India's multi-party system is a strength rather than a weakness. He contends that the nation is a coalition of diverse groups, and its democracy thrives when this diversity finds political representation. Jha warns against the temptation to view a mature democracy as one requiring simplified two-party structures or a single dominant narrative. He highlights that coalition governments compel national parties to negotiate, ensuring power remains answerable to the people rather than relying on a monopoly of legitimacy. The author distinguishes between majority rule, which grants a mandate to govern, and majoritarianism, which wrongly claims cultural or national superiority for the winning party. He asserts that the opposition and regional parties are essential institutions that allow the nation to hear competing aspirations. Ultimately, Jha states that democratic maturity means becoming comfortable with disagreement and protecting many cultures within a unified constitutional framework.
items.title: MP Manoj Kumar Jha argues India's multi-party system strengthens democracy
